name: terminal-mate
description: Save the terminal commands you type again and again, and run them with one click. Commands can ask you questions, run in a row, run later, or run from a keyboard shortcut.

scripts.shots: node test/shots/shoot.js . images && node test/shots/shoot.js . images gif

commands.title: TerminalMate: Open the Getting Started Guide

walkthroughs.title: Get started with TerminalMate
walkthroughs.description: Save the commands you type again and again, and run them with one click. Six short steps.

steps.title: Save your first command
steps.description:
Look at the status bar, the thin bar at the bottom of the window. The **TM** button opens your list of saved commands.

Choose **Add new command**, give it a name and type the command. Next time you only pick the name.

[Open my commands](command:terminal-mate.openCommands)

steps.title: Let a command ask you a question
steps.description:
Some part of a command is different every time: a branch name, a port, a message.

Write ``${input:Branch name}`` in that place. TerminalMate asks you for it each time and puts your answer into the command.

[Open my commands](command:terminal-mate.openCommands)

steps.title: Keep the list tidy
steps.description:
Point at a row in the list. Small buttons appear: move it up or down, schedule it, edit it, archive it, delete it.

The pencil also puts a command into a **group**, so related commands stay together under a heading.

[Open my commands](command:terminal-mate.openCommands)

steps.title: Chains and keyboard shortcuts
steps.description:
A **chain** runs saved commands one after another, for example Build and then Deploy. It stops when a step fails.

Any saved command or chain can also get its own keyboard shortcut.

[Open my commands](command:terminal-mate.openCommands)

steps.title: Run a command later
steps.description:
Run a command in 10 minutes, at 14:30, every 15 minutes or every day at 09:00.

The status bar counts down to the next run.

[Schedule a command](command:terminal-mate.scheduleCommand)

steps.title: Good to know
steps.description:
TerminalMate asks before it runs a risky command, remembers what you ran, and keeps your last command one click away.

[Show my history](command:terminal-mate.history)

[Open TerminalMate's settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22terminal-mate%22)

terminal-mate.customTerminals.markdownDescription:
Your saved commands. You normally do not edit this by hand: use the **TM** button in the status bar and **Add new command**.

Each item needs a `title` (the name you see in the list) and either a `command` (what to run) or a `chain` (names of saved commands to run one after another). Example:
```json
{ "title": "Amend", "command": "git commit --amend --no-verify" }
```

title.description: The name you see in the list. The terminal gets the same name. Chains and keyboard shortcuts find a command by this name.

command.markdownDescription:
What to type into the terminal. You can leave blanks that are filled in when the command runs:

- `${input:Label}` asks you to type a value
- `${pick:Label|one|two}` lets you choose from a list
- `${clipboard}` is the text you copied last
- `${workspaceFolder}` is the path of the open folder
- `${env:NAME}` is an environment variable

cwd.description: The folder the command runs in. Leave it out to use the folder you have open.

reuse.description: true: run in the terminal this command used before. false: open a new terminal every time. Leave it out to follow the "Reuse Terminal By Title" setting.

os.description: Show this command only on some systems: "win32" (Windows), "darwin" (macOS), "linux". One name or a list of names.

chain.description: Use instead of "command": the names of saved commands to run one after another in the same terminal. The chain stops at the first step that fails.

group.description: A group name. Commands with the same group are shown together under a heading in the list.

archived.description: true hides this command from the main list. It stays available under "Archive" at the bottom of the list.

terminal-mate.saveCommandsToWorkspace.markdownDescription:
Where new and changed commands are saved.

- Off: in your own settings. You see the same commands in every project.
- On: in `.vscode/settings.json` of the open folder. Only this project has them, and you can commit the file to share them with your team.

enumDescriptions: Your own order. Change it with the arrows on a row.
The command you used last comes first.
The command you use most often comes first.
terminal-mate.sortCommands.description: The order of commands in the list. Inside a group the same order is used.

terminal-mate.showStatusBar.description: Show TerminalMate's buttons in the status bar (the thin bar at the bottom of the window). When off, open the list with the command "TerminalMate: Open Saved Commands".

terminal-mate.customTerminalsButtonLabel.description: The text on the status bar button that opens your commands.

terminal-mate.pinLastCustomTerminal.description: Show a second status bar button with the command you ran last. One click runs it again.

terminal-mate.pinLastCustomTerminalLabel.description: The text in front of the command name on the "last command" button.

terminal-mate.reuseTerminalByTitle.description: On: a command runs in the terminal it used before, so you do not collect dozens of terminals. Off: every run opens a new terminal.

terminal-mate.confirmDangerousCommands.description: Ask "Continue?" before a risky command runs. Which commands count as risky is set in "Dangerous Command Patterns".

terminal-mate.dangerousCommandPatterns.markdownDescription:
Which commands count as risky. Out of the box: `git reset --hard`, `git clean -fd` and a force push.

Each line is a regular expression; upper and lower case do not matter. Add your own, for example `rm\s+-rf` or `drop\s+database`. (`\s+` means "one or more spaces". In `settings.json` write the backslash twice: `rm\\s+-rf`.)

terminal-mate.showPreviewForCustomTermin.description: Show the finished command in a window and wait for you to click "Run" before every run. Useful while you are still learning what your commands do.

terminal-mate.customHistorySize.description: How many of the commands you ran are kept in "TerminalMate: History".

terminal-mate.cursorSymbol.markdownDescription:
A marker for "stop here and let me type". TerminalMate types the command up to the marker and waits. You type the missing part in the terminal, then click **Finish snippet** in the status bar and the rest is added.

Example: `git commit -m "<|>" --no-verify`
